writeup: Genesis traces the family of Terah from Ur of the Chaldeans, a great city on the lower Euphrates, up the Fertile Crescent to Haran in upper Mesopotamia (Gen 11:31). There God calls Abram to leave his country and his father’s house for a land he will be shown, promising that through him all the families of the earth will be blessed (Gen 12:1–3).

Abram enters Canaan at Shechem and builds altars there and between Bethel and Ai before moving south into the Negeb. Famine drives him down to Egypt (Gen 12:10–20); he returns rich, parts from Lot, and settles by the oaks of Mamre at Hebron (Gen 13:18). Later he lives at Beersheba, from where he takes Isaac on the three-day journey to Moriah (Gen 22).

The route follows the arc of the Fertile Crescent rather than crossing the Syrian desert. The patriarchal period is traditionally dated c. 2000–1800 BC, but the dates are debated, and while Ur is usually identified with Tell el-Muqayyar in southern Iraq, a northern Ur near Haran has also been proposed.

writeup: After the tenth plague Israel sets out from Rameses in the eastern Nile delta (Exod 12:37). Rather than the short coastal road through Philistine territory, God leads the people by the wilderness road toward the Red Sea (Exod 13:17–18), where the waters are divided and Pharaoh’s army is drowned (Exod 14).

Through the wilderness of Shur and Sin — Marah, Elim, Rephidim — they reach Mount Sinai, where they receive the covenant and build the tabernacle (Exod 19–40). About a year later they move on to Kadesh-barnea; when they refuse to enter the land after the spies’ report, they wander for forty years (Num 13–14), finally going around Edom and Moab to the plains opposite Jericho (Num 20–22; 33). Joshua leads them across the Jordan (Josh 3–4).

Numbers 33 lists more than forty stopping places, most of which can no longer be identified. This map follows the traditional southern route with Sinai at Jebel Musa; scholars also propose a northern route or a Sinai in north-west Arabia, and the date of the Exodus (c. 1446 or c. 1270 BC) is likewise debated.

journeys.summary: Judah is deported along the Fertile Crescent to Babylon (597–586 BC); exiles return under Cyrus’ decree (538 BC onward).

legs.about: From Susa and Babylon back to Jerusalem under Cyrus’ decree (538–445 BC).

writeup: Babylon took captives from Judah in several waves: Daniel and other young nobles in 605 BC (Dan 1:1–6), King Jehoiachin, Ezekiel and the leading citizens in 597 BC (2 Kgs 24:10–16), and the bulk of the population after Jerusalem and the temple were destroyed in 586 BC. King Zedekiah was taken to Nebuchadnezzar’s headquarters at Riblah, blinded and carried to Babylon (2 Kgs 25:1–21).

The deportees did not cross the open desert but followed the Fertile Crescent north through Syria and down the Euphrates, a journey of some four months. In Babylonia they lived in their own communities, such as Tel-abib by the Chebar canal where Ezekiel prophesied (Ezek 3:15), and remembered Zion “by the rivers of Babylon” (Ps 137).

In 539 BC Cyrus of Persia took Babylon, and in 538 BC he allowed the Jews to return and rebuild the temple (Ezra 1:1–4). Groups returned under Sheshbazzar and Zerubbabel (538 BC), Ezra (458 BC, a four-month journey, Ezra 7:9) and Nehemiah, who came from the Persian court at Susa as governor (445 BC, Neh 2). The text does not give the return route; the caravan road by Tadmor and Damascus is a likely reconstruction.

journeys.name: Jesus’ Ministry
journeys.summary: From Bethlehem and Nazareth through the Galilean ministry to the cross and resurrection in Jerusalem.

legs.label: Ministry

waypoints.name: Mount Tabor (traditional)
waypoints.note: Transfiguration (traditional site; Mount Hermon also proposed).

legs.about: From his birth in Bethlehem to the cross and resurrection in Jerusalem.

writeup: Jesus is born in Bethlehem of Judea (Matt 2:1; Luke 2:4–7). Warned in a dream, Joseph takes the family to Egypt until Herod’s death, then settles in Nazareth in Galilee (Matt 2:13–23), where Jesus grows up.

After his baptism by John at the Jordan (Matt 3:13–17), Jesus makes Capernaum on the Sea of Galilee the base of his ministry (Matt 4:13), teaching and healing in the towns of Galilee. He passes through Samaria (John 4), travels north to the villages of Caesarea Philippi, where Peter confesses him as the Messiah (Matt 16:13–20), and is transfigured on a high mountain (Matt 17:1–8).

Setting his face toward Jerusalem (Luke 9:51), he goes by way of Jericho (Luke 19:1–10) and Bethany into the city, where he is crucified and rises again; the risen Jesus appears to two disciples on the road to Emmaus (Luke 24:13–35). John’s Gospel records several earlier visits to Jerusalem for the feasts, so this route is a simplified outline that follows the first three Gospels.

legs.about: Through Asia Minor to Troas, then into Europe: Macedonia and Achaia (c. AD 49–52).

waypoints.note: Three years; riot of the silversmiths.

waypoints.note: Three months in Greece; Romans written.

legs.about: Three years in Ephesus, then Macedonia and Greece, and by sea to Jerusalem (c. AD 53–57).

legs.label: Voyage to Rome (Acts 27–28)

waypoints.note: Transfer to an Alexandrian grain ship.

waypoints.name: Malta
waypoints.note: Shipwreck; three months on the island.

legs.about: From Caesarea as a prisoner; shipwrecked on Malta; Rome (c. AD 59–60).

writeup: Sent out by the church in Antioch of Syria (Acts 13:1–3), Paul — with Barnabas on the first journey, and Silas and Timothy on the second — carried the gospel along Roman roads and sea lanes. In each city he usually began in the synagogue before turning to the Gentiles, and he later wrote to many of the churches he founded.

The first journey crossed Cyprus into southern Asia Minor (c. AD 46–48). The second revisited those churches, crossed from Troas to Macedonia after a vision (Acts 16:9–10), and founded churches at Philippi, Thessalonica, Berea and Corinth (c. AD 49–52). The third centred on nearly three years in Ephesus before Paul revisited Macedonia and Greece and sailed for Jerusalem with the collection for its poor (c. AD 53–57).

Arrested in Jerusalem and held for two years at Caesarea, Paul appealed to Caesar and was sent to Rome under guard. After a storm and shipwreck on Malta (Acts 27–28) he reached Rome around AD 60, where he lived for two years under house arrest, teaching openly. The dates are approximate.

hebron_551.name: Hebron

dan_323.name: Dan
dan_323.description: The fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s maid (Gen. 30:6, “God hath judged me”, Heb. dananni).

hobah_571.name: Hobah

salem_1018.name: Salem

beer-lahai-roi_167.name: Beer-lahai-roi

gerar_459.description: A region; lodging-place, a very ancient town and district in the south border of Palestine, which was ruled over by a king named Abimelech (Gen. 10:19; 20:1, 2).

mahanaim_756.name: Mahanaim

machpelah_748.name: Machpelah

midian_796.description: An Arabian tribe descended from Midian. They inhabited principally the desert north of the peninsula of Arabia.

elim_369.name: Elim
elim_369.description: Trees, (Ex. 15:27; Num. 33:9), the name of the second station where the Israelites encamped after crossing the Red Sea.

rephidim_996.name: Rephidim

rehob_989.description: Another town of Asher (Josh. 19:30), kept possession of by the Canaanites (Judg. 1:31).

arnon_92.description: Swift, the southern boundary of the territory of Israel beyond Jordan, separating it from the land of Moab (Deut. 3:8, 16).

heshbon_565.description: Intelligence, a city ruled over by Sihon, king of the Amorites (Josh. 3:10; 13:17). It was taken by Moses (Num. 21:23-26), and became afterwards a Levitical city (Josh. 21:39) in the tribe of Reuben (Num. 32:37).

seir_1042.description: The name of a mountainous region occupied by the Edomites, extending along the eastern side of the Arabah from the south-eastern extremity of the Dead Sea to near the Akabah, or the eastern branch of the Red Sea.

mount_nebo_849.name: Mount Nebo
mount_nebo_849.description: A mountain in the land of Moab from which Moses looked for the first and the last time on the Promised Land (Deut. 32:49; 34:1).

shiloh_1081.name: Shiloh
shiloh_1081.description: Generally understood as denoting the Messiah, “the peaceful one,” as the word signifies (Gen. 49:10).

ai_36.name: Ai
ai_36.description: One of the royal cities of the Canaanites (Josh. 10:1; Gen. 12:8; 13:3). It was the scene of Joshua’s defeat, and afterwards of his victory.

shittim_1086.name: Shittim

gilgal_476.description: From the solemn transaction of the reading of the law in the valley of Shechem between Ebal and Gerizim the Israelites moved forward to Gilgal, and there made a permanent camp (Josh. 9:6; 10:6).

mount_ebal_832.name: Mount Ebal
mount_ebal_832.description: A mountain 3,076 feet above the level of the sea, and 1,200 feet above the level of the valley, on the north side of which stood the city of Shechem (q.v.).

gibeon_470.name: Gibeon
gibeon_470.description: Hill-city, “one of the royal cities, greater than Ai, and all the men thereof were mighty” (Josh. 10:2).

beth-horon_214.name: Beth-horon
beth-horon_214.description: House of the hollow, or of the cavern, the name of two towns or villages (2 Chr. 8:5; 1 Chr. 7:24) in the territory of Ephraim, on the way from Jerusalem to Joppa.

azekah_128.name: Azekah
azekah_128.description: Dug over, a town in the Shephelah or low hills of Judah (Josh. 15:35), where the five confederated Amoritish kings were defeated by Joshua and their army destroyed by a hailstrom (10:10, 11).

makkedah_760.name: Makkedah
makkedah_760.description: Herdsman’s place, one of the royal cities of the Canaanites (Josh. 12:16), near which was a cave where the five kings who had confederated against Israel sought refuge (10:10-29).

libnah_728.name: Libnah
libnah_728.description: One of the royal cities of the Canaanites taken by Joshua (Josh. 10:29-32; 12:15). It became one of the Levitical towns in the tribe of Judah (21:13), and was strongly fortified.

lachish_711.name: Lachish

eglon_361.name: Eglon
eglon_361.description: A city in Judah, near Lachish (Josh. 15:39). It was destroyed by Joshua (10:5, 6). It has been identified with Tell Nejileh, 6 miles south of Tell Hesy or Ajlan, north-west of Lachish.

hazor_545.name: Hazor

ramah_972.name: Ramah
ramah_972.description: A city first mentioned in Josh. 18:25, near Gibeah of Benjamin. It was fortified by Baasha, king of Israel (1 Kings 15:17-22; 2 Chr. 16:1-6).

gibeah_466.name: Gibeah
gibeah_466.description: A hill or hill-town, “of Benjamin” (1 Sam. 13:15), better known as “Gibeah of Saul” (11:4; Isa. 10:29).

kishon_705.name: Kishon

penuel_931.name: Penuel
penuel_931.description: Face of God, a place not far from Succoth, on the east of the Jordan and north of the river Jabbok.

zorah_1275.name: Zorah
zorah_1275.description: Place of wasps, a town in the low country of Judah, afterwards given to Dan (Josh. 19:41; Judg. 18:2), probably the same as Zoreah (Josh. 15:33).

timnah_1164.name: Timnah
timnah_1164.description: A town of Judah (Josh. 15:10). The Philistines took possession of it in the days of Ahaz (2 Chr. 28:18).

gaza_446.name: Gaza

kiriath-jearim_701.name: Kiriath-jearim
kiriath-jearim_701.description: City, a city belonging to Benjamin (Josh. 18:28), the modern Kuriet el-‘Enab, i.e., “city of grapes”, about 7 1/2 miles west-north-west of Jerusalem.

laish_713.name: Laish

jebus_629.name: Jebus

jerusalem_636.name: Jerusalem

ephrathah_404.name: Ephrathah
ephrathah_404.description: The ancient name of Bethlehem in Judah (Gen. 35:16, 19; 48:7).

ramah_975.name: Ramah
ramah_975.description: The same as Ramathaim-zophim (q.v.), a town of Mount Ephraim (1 Sam. 1:1, 19).

gath_442.name: Gath
gath_442.description: A wine-vat, one of the five royal cities of the Philistines (Josh. 13:3) on which the ark brought calamity (1 Sam. 5:8, 9; 6:17).

keilah_681.name: Keilah

ashdod_101.name: Ashdod

ekron_364.name: Ekron

zuph_1276.name: Zuph

geshur_461.name: Geshur

tyre_1184.description: A rock, now es-Sur; an ancient Phoenician city, about 23 miles, in a direct line, north of Acre, and 20 south of Sidon.

joppa_652.name: Joppa
joppa_652.description: Beauty, a town in the portion of Dan (Josh. 19:46; A.V., “Japho”), on a sandy promontory between Caesarea and Gaza, and at a distance of 30 miles north-west from Jerusalem.

jezreel_643.name: Jezreel
jezreel_643.description: A town of Issachar (Josh. 19:18), where the kings of Israel often resided (1 Kings 18:45; 21:1; 2 Kings 9:30).

abel-meholah_8.name: Abel-meholah
abel-meholah_8.description: Meadow of dancing, or the dancing-meadow, the birth-place and residence of the prophet Elisha, not far from Beth-shean (1 Kings 4:12), in the tribe of Issachar, near where the Wady el-Maleh emerges into the valley of the Jordan,…

assyria_111.name: Assyria
assyria_111.description: The name derived from the city Asshur on the Tigris, the original capital of the country, was originally a colony from Babylonia, and was ruled by viceroys from that kingdom.

damascus_322.name: Damascus
damascus_322.description: Activity, the most ancient of Oriental cities; the capital of Syria (Isa. 7:8; 17:3); situated about 133 miles to the north of Jerusalem.

gozan_492.name: Gozan
gozan_492.description: A region in Central Asia to which the Israelites were carried away captive (2 Kings 17:6; 1 Chr. 5:26; 2 Kings 19:12;

ecbatana_353.name: Ecbatana
ecbatana_353.description: (Ezra 6:2), called Ecbatana by classical writers, the capital of northern Media. Here was the palace which was the residence of the old Median monarchs, and of Cyrus and Cambyses.

nineveh_899.name: Nineveh
nineveh_899.description: First mentioned in Gen. 10:11, which is rendered in the Revised Version, “He [i.e., Nimrod] went forth into Assyria and builded Nineveh.” It is not again noticed till the days of Jonah, when it is described (Jonah 3:3; 4:11) as…

riblah_1001.name: Riblah
riblah_1001.description: Fruitful, an ancient town on the northern frontier of Palestine, 35 miles north-east of Baalbec, and 10 or 12 south of Lake Homs, on the eastern bank of the Orontes, in a wide and fertile plain.

carchemish_277.name: Carchemish
carchemish_277.description: Fortress of Chemosh, a city on the west bank of the Euphrates (Jer. 46:2; 2 Chr. 35:20), not, as was once supposed, the Circesium at the confluence of the Chebar and the Euphrates, but a city considerably higher up the river,…

holy_place_575.name: Holy Place
holy_place_575.description: One of the two portions into which the tabernacle was divided (Ex. 26:31; 37:17-25; Heb. 9:2).

megiddo_777.name: Megiddo
megiddo_777.description: Place of troops, originally one of the royal cities of the Canaanites (Josh. 12:21), belonged to the tribe of Manasseh (Judg. 1:27), but does not seem to have been fully occupied by the Israelites till the time of Solomon (1…

persia_938.name: Persia
persia_938.description: An ancient empire, extending from the Indus to Thrace, and from the Caspian Sea to the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf.

ahava_34.name: Ahava
ahava_34.description: Water, the river (Ezra 8:21) by the banks of which the Jewish exiles assembled under Ezra when about to return to Jerusalem from Babylon.

tadmor_1131.name: Tadmor
tadmor_1131.description: Palm, a city built by Solomon “in the wilderness” (2 Chr. 8:4).

dung_gate_346.name: Dung Gate
dung_gate_346.description: (Neh. 2:13), a gate of ancient Jerusalem, on the south-west quarter. “The gate outside of which lay the piles of sweepings and offscourings of the streets,” in the valley of Tophet.

water_gate_1230.name: Water Gate
water_gate_1230.description: The fruit of a species of palm (q.v.), the Phoenix dactilifera. This was a common tree in Palestine (Joel 1:12;

mizpah_811.name: Mizpah
mizpah_811.description: A city of Benjamin, “the watch-tower”, where the people were accustomed to meet in great national emergencies (Josh. 18:26;

geba_447.name: Geba
geba_447.description: The hill, (2 Sam. 5:25 [1 Chr. 14:16, “Gibeon”]; 2 Kings 23:8; Neh. 11:31), a Levitical city of Benjamin (1 Kings 15:22; 1 Sam. 13:16; 14:5, wrongly “Gibeah” in the A.V.), on the north border of Judah near Gibeah (Isa. 10:29;

ono_909.name: Ono
ono_909.description: A town of Benjamin, in the “plain of Ono” (1 Chr. 8:12; Ezra 2:33); now Kefr ‘Ana, 5 miles north of Lydda, and about 30 miles north-west of Jerusalem.

ophel_910.name: Ophel
ophel_910.description: Hill; mound, the long, narrow, rounded promontory on the southern slope of the temple hill, between the Tyropoeon and the Kedron valley (2 Chr. 27:3; 33:14;

susa_1118.name: Susa
susa_1118.description: A lily, the Susa of Greek and Roman writers, once the capital of Elam. It lay in the uplands of Susiana, on the east of the Tigris, about 150 miles to the north of the head of the Persian Gulf.

media_776.name: Media
media_776.description: Heb. Madai, which is rendered in the Authorized Version (1) “Madai,” Gen. 10:2; (2) “Medes,” 2 Kings 17:6; 18:11;

ethiopia_419.name: Ethiopia
ethiopia_419.description: Country of burnt faces; the Greek word by which the Hebrew Cush is rendered (Gen. 2:13; 2 Kings 19:9;

india_597.name: India
india_597.description: Occurs only in Esther 1:1 and 8:9, where the extent of the dominion of the Persian king is described.

uz_1190.name: Uz
uz_1190.description: Where Job lived (1:1; Jer. 25:20; Lam. 4:21), probably somewhere to the east or south-east of Palestine and north of Edom.

ophir_911.name: Ophir
ophir_911.description: Some region famous for its gold (1 Kings 9:28; 10:11; 22:48; Job 22:24; 28:16; Isa. 13:12).

sheba_1067.name: Sheba
sheba_1067.description: Heb. id. A kingdom in Arabia Felix. Sheba, in fact, was Saba in Southern Arabia, the Sabaeans of classical geography, who carried on the trade in spices with the other peoples of the ancient world.

teman_1150.name: Teman
teman_1150.description: A place in Southern Idumea, the land of “the sons of the east,” frequently mentioned in the Old Testament.

zion_1263.name: Zion
zion_1263.description: Sunny; height, one of the eminences on which Jerusalem was built.

lebanon_720.name: Lebanon
lebanon_720.description: White, “the white mountain of Syria,” is the loftiest and most celebrated mountain range in Syria.

mount_zion_860.name: Mount Zion
mount_zion_860.description: Sunny; height, one of the eminences on which Jerusalem was built.

michmash_793.name: Michmash
michmash_793.description: Something hidden, a town of Benjamin (Ezra 2:27), east of Bethel and south of Migron, on the road to Jerusalem (Isa. 10:28).

anathoth_63.name: Anathoth
anathoth_63.description: The name of one of the cities of refuge, in the tribe of Benjamin (Josh. 21:18).

geruth_chimham_460.name: Geruth Chimham
geruth_chimham_460.description: Pining, probably the youngest son of Barzillai the Gileadite (2 Sam. 19:37-40).

tel-abib_1143.name: Tel-abib
tel-abib_1143.description: Hill of corn, a place on the river Chebar, the residence of Ezekiel (Ezek. 3:15). The site is unknown.

chebar_283.name: Chebar
chebar_283.description: Length, a river in the “land of the Chaldeans” (Ezek. 1:3), on the banks of which were located some of the Jews of the Captivity (Ezek. 1:1; 3:15, 23; 10:15, 20, 22).

greece_495.name: Greece
greece_495.description: Orginally consisted of the four provinces of Macedonia, Epirus, Achaia, and Peleponnesus. In Acts 20:2 it designates only the Roman province of Macedonia.

ulai_1185.name: Ulai
ulai_1185.description: The Eulaus of the Greeks; a river of Susiana. It was probably the eastern branch of the Choasper (Kerkhan), which divided into two branches some 20 miles above the city of Susa.

beth-aven_191.name: Beth-aven
beth-aven_191.description: House of nothingness; i.e., “of idols”, a place in the mountains of Benjamin, east of Bethel (Josh. 7:2; 18:12; 1 Sam. 13:5).

tekoa_1142.name: Tekoa
tekoa_1142.description: Pitching of tents; fastening down, a town of Judah, about 12 miles south of Jerusalem, and visible from the city.

negeb_885.name: Negeb
negeb_885.description: Heb. Negeb, that arid district to the south of Palestine through which lay the caravan route from Central Palestine to Egypt (Gen. 12:9; 13:1, 3; 46:1-6).

gath-hepher_443.name: Gath-hepher
gath-hepher_443.description: Wine-press of the well, a town of Lower Galilee, about 5 miles from Nazareth; the birthplace of Jonah (2 Kings 14:25); the same as Gittah-hepher (Josh. 19:13).

tarshish_1139.name: Tarshish
tarshish_1139.description: The name of a place which first comes into notice in the days of Solomon. The question as to the locality of Tarshish has given rise to not a little discussion.

antioch_68.name: Antioch (Syria)
antioch_68.description: In Syria, on the river Orontes, about 16 miles from the Mediterranean, and some 300 miles north of Jerusalem.

galilee_433.name: Galilee
galilee_433.description: Circuit. Solomon rewarded Hiram for certain services rendered him by the gift of an upland plain among the mountains of Naphtali.

judea_657.name: Judea
judea_657.description: After the Captivity this name was applied to the whole of the country west of the Jordan (Hag. 1:1, 14; 2:2).

nazareth_878.name: Nazareth
nazareth_878.description: Separated, generally supposed to be the Greek form of the Hebrew netser, a “shoot” or “sprout.” Some, however, think that the name of the city must be connected with the name of the hill behind it, from which one of the finest…

capernaum_274.name: Capernaum
capernaum_274.description: Nahum’s town, a Galilean city frequently mentioned in the history of our Lord. It is not mentioned in the Old Testament.

rome_1013.name: Rome
rome_1013.description: The most celebrated city in the world at the time of Christ. It is said to have been founded B.C. 753.

bethany_186.name: Bethany
bethany_186.description: A village on the south-eastern slope of the Mount of Olives (Mark 11:1), about 2 miles east of Jerusalem, on the road to Jericho.

sidon_1093.name: Sidon
sidon_1093.description: A fishery, a town on the Mediterranean coast, about 25 miles north of Tyre. It received its name from the “first-born” of Canaan, the grandson of Noah (Gen. 10:15, 19).

decapolis_328.name: Decapolis
decapolis_328.description: Ten cities=deka, ten, and polis, a city, a district on the east and south-east of the Sea of Galilee containing “ten cities,” which were chiefly inhabited by Greeks.

bethsaida_231.name: Bethsaida
bethsaida_231.description: A city near which Christ fed 5,000 (Luke 9:10; comp. John 6:17; Matt. 14:15-21), and where the blind man had his sight restored (Mark 8:22), on the east side of the lake, two miles up the Jordan.

caesarea_philippi_267.name: Caesarea Philippi
caesarea_philippi_267.description: A city on the northeast of the marshy plain of el-Huleh, 120 miles north of Jerusalem, and 20 miles north of the Sea of Galilee, at the “upper source” of the Jordan, and near the base of Mount Hermon.

caesarea_266.name: Caesarea
caesarea_266.description: (Palestinae), a city on the shore of the Mediterranean, on the great road from Tyre to Egypt, about 70 miles northwest of Jerusalem, at the northern extremity of the plain of Sharon.

emmaus_382.name: Emmaus
emmaus_382.description: Hot baths, a village “three-score furlongs” from jerusalem, where our Lord had an interview with two of his disciples on the day of his resurrection (Luke 24:13).

ephesus_400.name: Ephesus
ephesus_400.description: The capital of proconsular Asia, which was the western part of Asia Minor. It was colonized principally from Athens.

cana_271.name: Cana
cana_271.description: Reedy, a town of Galilee, near Capernaum. Here our Lord wrought his first miracle, the turning of water into wine (John 2:1-11; 4:46).

sychar_1119.name: Sychar
sychar_1119.description: Liar or drunkard (see Isa. 28:1, 7), has been from the time of the Crusaders usually identified with Sychem or Shechem (John 4:5).

asia_108.name: Asia
asia_108.description: Is used to denote Proconsular Asia, a Roman province which embraced the western parts of Asia Minor, and of which Ephesus was the capital, in Acts 2:9; 6:9; 16:6; 19:10, 22; 20:4, 16, 18, etc., and probably Asia Minor in Acts…

azotus_132.name: Azotus
azotus_132.description: The Grecized form (Acts 8:40, etc.) of Ashdod (q.v.).

lydda_741.name: Lydda
lydda_741.description: A town in the tribe of Ephraim, mentioned only in the New Testament (Acts 9:32, 35, 38) as the scene of Peter’s miracle in healing the paralytic AEneas.

seleucia_1045.name: Seleucia
seleucia_1045.description: The sea-port of Antioch, near the mouth of the Orontes. Paul and his companions sailed from this port on their first missionary journey (Acts 13:4).

salamis_1016.name: Salamis
salamis_1016.description: A city on the south-east coast of Cyprus (Acts 13:5), where Saul and Barnabas, on their first missionary journey, preached the word in one of the Jewish synagogues, of which there seem to have been several in that place.

paphos_919.name: Paphos
paphos_919.description: The capital of the island of Cyprus, and therefore the residence of the Roman governor. It was visited by Paul and Barnabas on their first missionary tour (Acts 13:6).

perga_936.name: Perga
perga_936.description: The capital of Pamphylia, on the coast of Asia Minor. Paul and his companions landed at this place from Cyprus on their first missionary journey (Acts 13:13, 14), and here Mark forsook the party and returned to Jerusalem.

antioch_69.name: Antioch (Pisidia)
antioch_69.description: In the extreme north of Pisidia; was visited by Paul and Barnabas on the first missionary journey (Acts 13:14).

iconium_590.name: Iconium
iconium_590.description: The capital of ancient Lycaonia. It was first visited by Paul and Barnabas from Antioch-in-Pisidia during the apostle’s first missionary journey (Acts 13:50, 51).

lystra_742.name: Lystra
lystra_742.description: A town of Lycaonia, in Asia Minor, in a wild district and among a rude population. Here Paul preached the gospel after he had been driven by persecution from Iconium (Acts 14:2-7).

derbe_330.name: Derbe
derbe_330.description: A small town on the eastern part of the upland plain of Lycaonia, about 20 miles from Lystra.

troas_1182.name: Troas
troas_1182.description: A city on the coast of Mysia, in the north-west of Asia Minor, named after ancient Troy, which was at some little distance from it (about 4 miles) to the north.

neapolis_880.name: Neapolis
neapolis_880.description: New city, a town in Thrace at which Paul first landed in Europe (Acts 16:11). It was the sea-port of the inland town of Philippi, which was distant about 10 miles.

philippi_942.name: Philippi
philippi_942.description: Formerly Crenides, “the fountain,” the capital of the province of Macedonia. It stood near the head of the Sea, about 8 miles north-west of Kavalla.

thessalonica_1158.name: Thessalonica
thessalonica_1158.description: A large and populous city on the Thermaic bay. It was the capital of one of the four Roman districts of Macedonia, and was ruled by a praetor.

berea_177.name: Berea
berea_177.description: A city of Macedonia to which Paul with Silas and Timotheus went when persecuted at Thessalonica (Acts 17:10, 13), and from which also he was compelled to withdraw, when he fled to the sea-coast and thence sailed to Athens (14,…

athens_118.name: Athens
athens_118.description: The capital of Attica, the most celebrated city of the ancient world, the seat of Greek literature and art during the golden period of Grecian history.

corinth_306.name: Corinth
corinth_306.description: A Grecian city, on the isthmus which joins the Peloponnesus to the mainland of Greece. It is about 48 miles west of Athens.

galatia_431.name: Galatia
galatia_431.description: Has been called the “Gallia” of the East, Roman writers calling its inhabitants Galli. They were an intermixture of Gauls and Greeks, and hence were called Gallo-Graeci, and the country Gallo-Graecia.

macedonia_747.name: Macedonia
macedonia_747.description: In New Testament times, was a Roman province lying north of Greece. It was governed by a propraetor with the title of proconsul.

assos_110.name: Assos
assos_110.description: A sea-port town of Proconsular Asia, in the district of Mysia, on the north shore of the Gulf of Adramyttium.

miletus_801.name: Miletus
miletus_801.description: (Miletum, 2 Tim. 4:20), a seaport town and the ancient capital of Ionia, about 36 miles south of Ephesus.

rhodes_1000.name: Rhodes
rhodes_1000.description: A rose, an island to the south of the western extremity of Asia Minor, between Coos and Patara, about 46 miles long and 18 miles broad.

myra_864.name: Myra
myra_864.description: One of the chief towns of Lycia, in Asia Minor, about 2 1/2 miles from the coast (Acts 27:5).

fair_havens_424.name: Fair Havens
fair_havens_424.description: A harbour in the south of Crete, some 5 miles to the east of which was the town of Lasea (Acts 27:8).

melita_761.name: Melita
melita_761.description: (Acts 27:28), an island in the Mediterranean, the modern Malta. Here the ship in which Paul was being conveyed a prisoner to Rome was wrecked.

syracuse_1121.name: Syracuse
syracuse_1121.description: A city on the south-east coast of Sicily, where Paul landed and remained three days when on his way to Rome (Acts 28:12).

rhegium_999.name: Rhegium
rhegium_999.description: Breach, a town in the south of Italy, on the Strait of Messina, at which Paul touched on his way to Rome (Acts 28:13).

puteoli_963.name: Puteoli
puteoli_963.description: A city on the coast of Campania, on the north shore of a bay running north from the Bay of Naples, at which Paul landed on his way to Rome, from which it was distant 170 miles.

spain_1111.name: Spain
spain_1111.description: Paul expresses his intention (Rom. 15:24, 28) to visit Spain. There is, however, no evidence that he ever carried it into effect, although some think that he probably did so between his first and second imprisonment.

cenchreae_281.name: Cenchreae
cenchreae_281.description: Millet, the eastern harbour of Corinth, from which it was distant about 9 miles east, and the outlet for its trade with the Asiatic shores of the Mediterranean.

achaia_16.name: Achaia
achaia_16.description: The name originally of a narrow strip of territory in Greece, on the north-west of the Peloponnesus.

arabia_80.name: Arabia
arabia_80.description: Arabia Petraea, i.e., the Rocky Arabia, so called from its rocky mountains and stony plains.

colossae_305.name: Colossae
colossae_305.description: Or Colosse, a city of Phrygia, on the Lycus, which is a tributary of the Maeander. It was about 12 miles above Laodicea, and near the great road from Ephesus to the Euphrates, and was consequently of some mercantile importance.

laodicea_716.name: Laodicea
laodicea_716.description: The city of this name mentioned in Scripture lay on the confines of Phrygia and Lydia, about 40 miles east of Ephesus (Rev. 3:14), on the banks of the Lycus.

hierapolis_569.name: Hierapolis
hierapolis_569.description: Sacred city, a city of Phrygia, where was a Christian church under the care of Epaphras (Col. 4:12, 13).

nicopolis_894.name: Nicopolis
nicopolis_894.description: City of victory, where Paul intended to winter (Titus 3:12). There were several cities of this name.

crete_310.name: Crete
crete_310.description: Now called Candia, one of the largest islands in the Meditterranean, about 140 miles long and 35 broad.

pontus_956.name: Pontus
pontus_956.description: A province of Asia Minor, stretching along the southern coast of the Euxine Sea, corresponding nearly to the modern province of Trebizond.

cappadocia_276.name: Cappadocia
cappadocia_276.description: The easternmost and the largest province of Asia Minor. Christianity very early penetrated into this country (1 Pet. 1:1).

bithynia_250.name: Bithynia
bithynia_250.description: A province in Asia Minor, to the south of the Euxine and Propontis. Christian congregations were here formed at an early time (1 Pet. 1:1).

patmos_926.name: Patmos
patmos_926.description: A small rocky and barren island, one of the group called the “Sporades,” in the AEgean Sea.

thyatira_1160.name: Thyatira
thyatira_1160.description: A city of Asia Minor, on the borders of Lydia and Mysia. Its modern name is Ak-hissar, i.e., “white castle.” Here was one of the seven churches (Rev. 1:11; 2:18-28).

sardis_1027.name: Sardis
sardis_1027.description: The metropolis of Lydia in Asia Minor. It stood on the river Pactolus, at the foot of mount Tmolus.

pergamum_937.name: Pergamum
pergamum_937.description: The chief city of Mysia, in Asia Minor. One of the “seven churches” was planted here (Rev. 1:11; 2:17).

smyrna_1103.name: Smyrna
smyrna_1103.description: Myrrh, an ancient city of Ionia, on the western coast of Asia Minor, about 40 miles to the north of Ephesus.

philadelphia_941.name: Philadelphia
philadelphia_941.description: Brotherly love, a city of Lydia in Asia Minor, about 25 miles south-east of Sardis. It was the seat of one of the “seven churches” (Rev. 3:7-12).

ur_1189.name: Ur of the Chaldees
ur_1189.description: Light, or the moon city, a city “of the Chaldees,” the birthplace of Haran (Gen. 11:28, 31), the largest city of Shinar or northern Chaldea, and the principal commercial centre of the country as well as the centre of political…

moriah_821.name: Moriah
moriah_821.description: The chosen of Jehovah. Some contend that Mount Gerizim is meant, but most probably we are to regard this as one of the hills of Jerusalem.

nebo_883.name: Nebo
nebo_883.description: A Chaldean god whose worship was introduced into Assyria by Pul (Isa. 46:1; Jer. 48:1). To this idol was dedicated the great temple whose ruins are still seen at Birs Nimrud.

tabor_1128.name: Tabor (Mountain)
tabor_1128.description: Now Jebel et-Tur, a cone-like prominent mountain, 11 miles west of the Sea of Galilee. It is about 1,843 feet high.
